articles.title: Track Renewal Works on Rochdale Line Affecting Services Until 28 August
articles.excerpt: From 15 to 28 August, tram services on the Rochdale line will be disrupted due to track renewal works, with a bus replacement service in operation.
articles.content_html:
Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has announced that track renewal works will take place on the Rochdale line from Saturday 15 August until Friday 28 August. During this period, tram services will be disrupted, and a bus replacement service will operate between the affected stops.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the bus replacement service will help maintain connectivity during the works. Further details regarding the specific stops affected can be found on the TfGM travel alerts page.

In addition to the track works, essential improvement works are also scheduled at Prestwich Metrolink stop until 12 October. Tram services will not be affected at this stop, but there will be an increased presence of staff to assist passengers.

Currently, the lifts at Failsworth and Etihad Campus tram stops are out of service, meaning there is no step-free access at these locations. Passengers needing assistance should contact the Metrolink customer service centre at 0161 244 1000 for journey planning support.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Set to Face Crawley Town in Upcoming Match
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC will take on Crawley Town in a highly anticipated match this weekend, following Crawley's recent performance against Crewe.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC is preparing to face Crawley Town this weekend in a match that promises to be an exciting encounter for local football fans. The game is set to take place at the Crown Oil Arena, with kick-off scheduled for Saturday, August 21, 2026.

Crawley Town midfielder Klaudio Krasniqi has expressed optimism following his team's recent loss to Crewe, stating that there are 'plenty of positives' to take from the match as they head into the fixture against Rochdale. This sentiment may boost the Crawley squad as they look to secure a win on the road.

For Rochdale, this match presents an opportunity to build momentum in the league after a challenging start to the season. The team will be looking to leverage home advantage to secure vital points.

Fans are encouraged to attend and support their teams, as local football continues to play a significant role in community engagement and pride. Tickets are available through the club's official website.

articles.title: Rochdale Council to Stagger Backpay for Universal Credit Staff
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council will implement a staggered payment system for backdated wages to prevent staff on Universal Credit from losing benefits, following concerns raised by UNISON.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has announced a change in its payment system for backdated wages for staff receiving Universal Credit. This decision follows concerns raised by UNISON that lump-sum payments were negatively impacting these employees' benefits.

The new staggered payment approach aims to prevent reductions in Universal Credit as a result of backpay. This change is expected to provide financial relief to those affected by the previous payment method.

The council's decision reflects an awareness of the challenges faced by employees on Universal Credit, particularly regarding sudden changes in income.

Further details on the implementation of this new payment system are expected to be released in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Lift at Derker Tram Stop Out of Service Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Alternative routes are available for step-free access to platforms.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 20 August 2026, impacting accessibility for passengers. The lift has been unavailable since 5:38pm on that date, and there is no specified date for when it will be repaired.

For customers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading towards Rochdale can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, but must cross the tracks to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has advised that they are sorry for any inconvenience caused by this disruption. Passengers are encouraged to plan their journeys accordingly and consider alternative routes if necessary.

Further updates regarding the lift's status will be provided as they become available. For more information, passengers can check the Transport for Greater Manchester website.
